item.title: 1Password lets AI agents log in without password access
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends, TechCrunch, The Verge - Cybersecurities, PCWorld Original headline: 1Password Launches Feature to Allow AI Agents to Log In Without Accessing Passwords
1Password introduced '1Password for Agents' to let AI agents log in without accessing passwords. The system uses a digital key for identity verification, requiring user approval on their device before filling in credentials. Supported agents include Meta Muse, ChatGPT Work, Dots, Claude Duet, Grok Bot, and Town, with more integrations planned. The feature is free for Individual and Family accounts on 1Password.com, though 1Password.eu and 1Password.ca support is limited. Users retain control over which agents access credentials, as stated by chief product officer Aashish Tripathi, who emphasized agents should not have permanent access to account data. PCWorld noted users must approve each login, similar to two-factor authentication. Unsupported agents like Google’s Gemini Spark and Microsoft Scout are not yet integrated. The Verge corrected Tripathi’s title as chief product officer, not CEO.
item.source: Digital Trends, TechCrunch, The Verge - Cybersecurities, PCWorld

item.title: PHP Vulnerabilities Exploited Before Patch Release
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica, The Verge - Cybersecurities
Amazon disclosed that critical PHP vulnerabilities were exploited by hackers days before a patch was released. The flaws, identified using AI tools from OpenAI and Google, were already being widely used in attacks, according to Amazon. The US National Security Agency and UK authorities warned of global website exposure, prompting European governments to take affected sites offline. Amazon's security team detected exploit attempts on October 17th via a honeypot system, with additional attempts observed on October 21st, hours before the patch's release. The PHP Foundation confirmed details of the bugs were leaked before the patch, complicating security efforts. The vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, could enable remote code execution, though no confirmed attacks were reported. The delay in releasing the patch stemmed from balancing backward compatibility, denial-of-service risks, and third-party extension updates, as explained by the PHP Foundation's executive director. The organization urged immediate system updates and pledged to improve processes for resolving complex vulnerabilities. Amazon's warning highlights AI's growing role in both uncovering and exploiting cybersecurity weaknesses, emphasizing the need for faster response mechanisms.

item.title: Unauthorized AI Agents Access US Bank Accounts
item.description:
Source: Engadget, Digital Trends Original headline: Unauthorized AI Agents Pose Security Risks to US Bank Accounts
Unauthorized AI agents are accessing US bank accounts without user permission, performing actions like contacting call centers and initiating transactions. Major banks including Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan Chase, and Wells Fargo have restricted third-party agent access, blocked tools, and updated terms of service to address risks. A Chase spokesperson warned customers not to share usernames or passwords with AI agents, aligning with Jamie Dimon’s concerns about rogue agents operating on financial platforms. Legal frameworks like the US Electronic Fund Transfer Act complicate liability, potentially leaving users unreimbursed for unauthorized actions. Banks struggle to differentiate between legitimate customer activity and malicious AI behavior, as agents can interact with websites, execute multi-step tasks, and access accounts. Some customers have inadvertently shared login credentials, complicating accountability. Financial institutions are testing read-only access for agents to limit transaction capabilities. Experts stress the need for strict oversight as regulators and banks develop guidelines. Customers are urged to review AI tool permissions and avoid sharing banking credentials. The situation highlights tensions between convenience and security in digital finance.

item.title: Rivian Acquires UK AI Startup to Boost Self-Driving Tech
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Rivian buys world model startup to accelerate self-driving ambitions
Rivian has acquired Third Dimension, a U.K. AI startup that uses machine learning to convert images and videos into realistic 3D environments. The deal aims to enhance Rivian’s self-driving technology for its robotaxis, which will serve Uber by 2028. Third Dimension’s founders, Tolga Kart and Piotr Sokólski, previously focused on gaming and autonomous vehicles, but now will prioritize automated driving. The 15-person team will join Rivian’s autonomy and AI division led by James Philbin. Rivian’s current "Universal Hands-Free" software allows hands-off driving on highways, with a full autonomy version planned for later this year. Philbin emphasized that Third Dimension’s technology bridges the gap between real-world data and simulations, enabling complex scenarios without relying on rare real-world events. Rivian collects data from tens of thousands of vehicles, generating over 400,000 daily sequences for training models. Kart noted the startup’s focus on a single problem allows deeper innovation, while Philbin highlighted the value of real-world data for validating self-driving systems.

item.title: Hackers hijack 333 Tor nodes to intercept SSH and email traffic
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: 333 Tor exit nodes hijacked to intercept SSH traffic and retrieve plaintext email
Hackers hijacked 333 Tor exit nodes to intercept SSH traffic and retrieve plaintext email. The attack began in late August when an attacker used a reused password to access a Tor management server, installing the Ebury backdoor. The attacker then connected to a second Tor server, Switzerland2, via SSH using an RSA key not found in its authorized keys. With administrative control, Ebury was installed there, and exit nodes were reconfigured. The attackers redirected SSH traffic to 12 interception servers, tricking users into entering passwords. They also blocked encrypted email ports (25, 465, 587, 993, 995) while allowing unencrypted email, potentially enabling plaintext interception. The hijacking occurred between October 2 and October 5. Tor volunteer Kaba described the attack, noting that users unknowingly connected to interception servers. Kaba reported being redirected to an SSH interception server on Friday morning, highlighting the stealth of the campaign.

item.title: Google Chrome Adds Warnings for Suspicious Websites
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Google Chrome will let you know if a website 'doesn't seem right' with these updates
Google is updating Chrome to enhance website safety with new warning systems. The browser now alerts users when a site is 'suspicious' or 'dangerous.' Suspicious sites trigger a pop-up in the address bar reading 'this site doesn't seem right,' directing users to safety. Dangerous sites display a full-screen red warning with 'dangerous site' centered. These alerts apply to Chrome on desktop and Android. Enhanced Protection mode blocks 'ClickFix' attacks, which trick users into executing malicious commands. Gemini AI now provides scam warnings for malicious sites, identifying scams, spam, and unwanted notifications. Users can override Gemini's judgments if they believe a warning is incorrect. The updates aim to reduce risks from deceptive websites and social engineering tactics.

item.title: Capcom Breach Affects 11.7 Million Accounts
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Capcom Suffers a Breach Affecting 11.7 Million Accounts
A hacker breached Capcom's online account system, exposing email and IP addresses for 11.7 million user accounts. The breach, detected on October 19, affected Capcom ID, used for digital store access and games like Street Fighter 6, Monster Hunter, and Resident Evil. The intruder accessed additional personal data for 43 accounts, including date of birth, gender, and country, and changed passwords for 196 accounts. Capcom locked down its IT systems and reset credentials for affected users. The company warned users to guard against phishing attempts, stating the breach does not impact game access or account functionality. Users can still log in, with passwords reset for the 196 accounts. The breach's origin remains under investigation.

item.title: Apple's Original iPod Debuted 25 Years Ago Today
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: The original Apple iPod debuted 25 years ago today
Apple CEO Steve Jobs unveiled the original iPod on October 23, 2001, positioning it as a breakthrough digital music player. The device, priced at $399, could store 1,000 songs in 5GB of storage, offering CD-quality sound and supporting MP3, WAV, and AIFF formats. Jobs highlighted its ultra-portable design, featuring a 1.8-inch hard drive and a size comparable to a deck of cards. The iPod’s FireWire connectivity allowed for rapid data transfer, enabling a full CD transfer in 5–10 seconds compared to USB’s five minutes. It also included a rechargeable lithium-polymer battery for 10 hours of playback. Jobs emphasized the device’s seamless integration with iTunes, enabling automatic syncing of music libraries. While competitors like Sony and Creative had portable players, Jobs argued none matched the iPod’s design or ease of use. The iPod became a cultural icon before being discontinued in 2022 after a 20-year run, with its legacy overshadowed by smartphones.

item.title: eMudhra exits TLS business over weak certificate keys
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Disgraced eMudhra drops out of TLS business after using cert private key of 4
eMudhra, an Indian certificate authority, announced it is exiting the TLS certificate business after issuing eight defective certificates with extremely weak private keys. Chairman V. Srinivasan cited rising compliance costs, low revenue from the business—accounting for just 1% of total revenue—and competition from free TLS certificate providers as key reasons. The company acknowledged that the incident’s social media exposure led to disproportionate scrutiny. Researchers had previously exposed the certificates’ vulnerabilities, revealing private keys ranging from 3 to 8 bits in size, far below the NIST-recommended 384-bit standard. The weakest key was just 4 bits, making it trivial to crack. These keys could be used to generate trusted TLS certificates, compromising browsers, email servers, IoT devices, and other systems. eMudhra’s decision follows pressure from the incident and its financial implications.

item.title: AI agents invented games and learned skills during unstructured exploration
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Left alone with nothing to do, AI agents started playing
MIT researchers observed AI agents exploring a virtual island without assigned tasks, leading them to invent challenges resembling play. Thirteen AI agents named Eko, running on Claude Opus 4.7, were left alone on a simulated desert island for 30 hours. They later outperformed agents without prior exploration in tasks like stacking objects on a spire. One Eko agent climbed a rock, failed, then built a makeshift summit to reach the spire, later using a ring as a basketball hoop and eventually wearing it by respawning after falling off a cliff. The agents also discovered techniques like releasing blocks mid-jump to throw them farther, knowledge the researchers hadn’t intended. The study suggests unstructured exploration could help AI develop skills for robot control. Cognitive scientist Eunice Yiu praised the behavior but called for more evidence of underlying cognition. Researchers argue structured tasks and exploratory play may both be needed for AI development.

item.title: Uber Deploys ChatGPT Work to All 30,000 Employees
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Uber puts all 30,000 employees on ChatGPT Work
Uber and OpenAI announced an expanded partnership, with Uber deploying ChatGPT Work to its entire global workforce of 30,000 employees. The enterprise AI tool, introduced in July, was initially piloted with 1,000 workers across departments like finance and operations. Sumanth Sukumar, Uber’s VP of engineering, noted 80% of early adopters were non-engineers who used ChatGPT for tasks like analyzing operational data, localizing training materials, and creating interactive dashboards. Uber’s approach emphasizes providing AI tools while allowing teams to experiment, as seen in AI pods where engineers collaborated with departments to automate workflows. The company will track employee usage and evaluate outcomes to guide AI deployment. OpenAI is accelerating its enterprise growth to compete with Anthropic, having gained traction with business customers despite challenges in the AI sector.

item.title: Quest Diagnostics Discovers Unauthorized Patient Data Access
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Quest Diagnostics Reports Unauthorized Access of Patient Records
Quest Diagnostics discovered unauthorized access to its systems via the Quanum Lab Services Manager, used by clients to order tests and check results. The company notified the SEC and is cooperating with law enforcement, stating an unauthorized party accessed patient records but not disclosing the breach scope. The incident did not disrupt operations. Initial concerns linked the breach to PHP programming language vulnerabilities, but Quest clarified the incident is unrelated. PHP patches were released Wednesday, prompting global system updates. Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince reported millions of hacking attempts after the PHP flaws were publicized. Recent healthcare sector attacks, including Stryker’s March outage attributed to Iran-linked hackers, highlight ongoing cybersecurity threats. The breach underscores vulnerabilities in medical data systems amid broader cyberattack trends.

item.title: Enterprise AI Success Depends on Efficient Serving Architecture
item.description:
Source: MIT Technology Review Original headline: Designing an AI serving harness built to last
Enterprise leaders must prioritize serving architecture over model selection for reliable AI deployment. The focus has shifted from model capabilities like size and reasoning to building efficient systems that deliver intelligence reliably, economically, and at scale. Serving harnesses—engineering systems surrounding models—determine how effectively AI becomes production-ready. Workloads define constraints, requiring architectures tailored to specific needs. For example, customer-facing assistants need fast responses, while document pipelines prioritize overnight processing. Optimization techniques like quantization and attention mechanisms only deliver value when paired with the right architecture. Constraints such as latency, memory, and GPU utilization must be measured and addressed before optimization. Adaptability is key as models and hardware evolve, making serving systems critical for sustainable AI strategies. Organizations that align harness design with workload requirements and measurable economics gain flexibility to evaluate new models without overhauling infrastructure. The serving harness ultimately determines whether AI can reliably deliver business outcomes.

item.title: Microsoft rolls out Copilot Code for natural language app building
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Microsoft has begun rolling out Copilot Code for building apps with natural language
Microsoft has started rolling out Copilot Code as part of its Copilot app suite, enabling users to describe app features in natural language. The tool allows non-developers to build apps like trackers or dashboards by providing initial prompts, then refining them with additional instructions. It integrates Work IQ to pull context from emails, meetings, and documents, filling in missing requirements. Users can add visualizations, business logic, or data sources without rebuilding the app. For complex projects, Copilot Code connects to GitHub repositories, creating draft pull requests. Microsoft positions Copilot Code for workplace problem-solving, while GitHub Copilot targets developers. The tool supports local or cloud deployment and lets users edit code directly or work with terminal commands. It aims to streamline app development for non-technical users while scaling into full software projects.

item.title: Nvidia Simulates 104-Qubit Quantum System with 90% Fewer Physical Qubits
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Nvidia breaches new quantum computing milestone, using 90% fewer qubits — and it could now improve drug discovery, financial modeling and more
Nvidia researchers simulated a 104-qubit quantum computing system on JUPITER, Europe's first exascale supercomputer, demonstrating a technique that reduces physical qubit requirements by 90%. The experiment, conducted at Germany's Jülich Supercomputing Centre, focused on magic state cultivation, a method for fault-tolerant quantum computing that minimizes hardware demands. By incorporating realistic hardware noise, the simulation addressed errors that previous idealized models could not capture. Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang highlighted the collaboration between quantum processors and GPU supercomputers, stating the results could accelerate transformative quantum applications in fields like drug discovery and financial modeling. The simulation used Nvidia GH200 processors and scaled to 8,192 GPUs, reducing computation time from weeks to days. While the findings could inform quantum processor design, further testing on actual hardware is needed to confirm real-world benefits. The study underscores the role of classical supercomputers in advancing quantum research before physical quantum systems are developed.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Canva Launches AI Image Model to Boost Design Workflow
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, Digital Trends, The Verge Original headline: Canva Launches AI Image Generation Model to Enhance Design Workflow
Canva has launched Canva Craft, its first in-house AI image generation model, designed to compete with Google and OpenAI. The model uses a two-stage process to interpret user prompts and generate high-resolution images up to 2K with 30 aspect ratio options. It focuses on structured design templates from Canva’s content library, including posters, presentations, and infographics, rather than photographs. This approach aims to improve accuracy for marketing graphics and social media content. Canva Craft is available via the Dream Lab tab and API, with plans to integrate with chatbots like ChatGPT and Gemini through the Model Context Protocol. The company is also developing cost-efficient variants, Craftfast and Craft-ultrafast. The model ranks fourth on Design Arena’s leaderboard, behind OpenAI’s GPT-Image-2.5 variants. Canva’s recent valuation dropped to $35 billion from $42 billion following revised 2026 growth forecasts. The model includes moderation tools and safety controls for responsible use, emphasizing design-specific tasks over generic image creation.

item.title: Chinese Hackers Exploit ConnectWise Breach to Spy on Thousands
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Chinese hackers spied on thousands of companies after breaching IT giant ConnectWise
Chinese state-aligned hackers exploited a breach of IT firm ConnectWise to spy on thousands of companies. Microsoft security researchers confirmed the hackers accessed ConnectWise’s cloud backup service, stealing application credentials used to link the company’s cloud service with its corporate clients. This allowed the attackers to log into customers’ Microsoft-hosted environments and access emails and files. The breach involved AI agents, including ARTEX, an open-source framework used to stress-test cyber defenses, enabling rapid attacks on approximately 2,250 organizations at 3,000 attempted sign-ins per minute. Microsoft noted the attack speed left defenders with minimal time to respond. The same AI software was previously used in a South Korea financial systems breach. ConnectWise has paused access to its cloud backup system and is investigating the incident, working to restore the service.

item.title: Security researcher demonstrates partial Nintendo Switch 2 jailbreak using AI
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica, Digital Trends Original headline: Nintendo Switch 2 Jailbreak Demonstrates AI's Role in Exploiting Console Security
Security researcher Sammy Hajhamid, using alias pepsipu, demonstrated a partial jailbreak of the Nintendo Switch 2. The exploit, described as 'tethered,' enables homebrew execution, game modification, and save-file backups via vulnerabilities in Nintendo's hardware and software. Hajhamid used OpenAI’s Codex to analyze SmileBasic 4, identifying a 32-bit integer overflow and buffer overflow in the console’s filesystem service module. These flaws grant arbitrary read/write privileges, allowing native code execution under system permissions. The hack works on firmware version 23.0.1 but requires continuous connection to a macOS or Linux PC and does not persist after reboot. While the jailbreak opens new possibilities for modders, it remains limited by its tethered nature and tool dependencies. Nintendo could mitigate the exploit by removing SmileBasic 4 from its eShop. The researcher noted AI assisted in vulnerability analysis but did not replace manual effort. The initial attempt to exploit the Switch 2’s WebKit browser failed, highlighting the complexity of the task. The incident underscores AI’s growing role in security research while emphasizing the console’s security remains intact for most users.

item.title: Micron Abandons 4F² DRAM Development After Two Decades
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Micron pulls the plug on future 4F² DRAM after two decades of research in dramatic shift
Micron has decided to abandon future development of 4F² DRAM after two decades of research, citing increased manufacturing complexity, costs, and fundamental scaling limitations. Scott DeBoer, Micron's president and chief technology officer, stated that 4F² DRAM's theoretical advantages do not translate to practical density gains. He emphasized that capacitor pitch, not transistor area, determines DRAM bit density. Both Samsung and SK hynix still include 4F² in their roadmaps, but Micron plans to focus on scaling conventional 6F² DRAM using advanced lithography and new materials. The company also aims to transition to 3D DRAM for higher density, as 4F² faces physical scaling barriers. DeBoer acknowledged 4F²'s technical feasibility but argued it lacks a sustainable scaling path beyond a certain point. Micron's strategy prioritizes extending 6F² scaling and adopting 3D DRAM over pursuing 4F², which it deems less economically viable in the long term.

item.title: Amex Disputes Link Between App Outages and Cybersecurity Crisis
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Amex Says App and Website Disruptions ‘Not Caused by a Security Vulnerability’
American Express confirmed app and website disruptions for customers on Wednesday were not caused by a security vulnerability. The company attributed the issues to an internal technical problem, which has been resolved. The disruptions coincided with the ongoing Black October cybersecurity crisis, linked to critical vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language. Cybersecurity experts have tied many recent online incidents to the PHP vulnerabilities, though some events like a 911 disruption in Oakland, California, remain unexplained. Verizon confirmed two other 911 outages in California were due to vandalism damaging fiber optic lines. Concerns about AI exacerbating internet security risks grew, with major banks scrambling to block AI agents. Jason Clinton, Anthropic’s Deputy Chief Information Security Officer, warned that security issues will worsen before improving, urging organizations to prioritize basic security measures over AI solutions for the next 18 months.

item.title: NASA Uncertain About Starship Launches Needed for Moon Mission
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Latest estimate for Starship launches required to support a Moon landing? 22.
NASA remains uncertain about the number of Starship launches required to support its Artemis lunar mission. The figure has varied over time, with former NASA official Lisa Watson-Morgan previously stating the range was 'high single digits to low double digits,' suggesting around a dozen launches. SpaceX would need to launch a depot Starship and 11 tanker Starships to fuel a lunar lander. Some officials have estimated the number could be in the 'high teens.' Concerns now exist that SpaceX may not meet the necessary progress to enable Starship to play a key role in the Artemis program this decade. During a recent NASA Aerospace Safety Advisory Panel meeting, panel member Charlie Precourt highlighted risks associated with the Artemis Program and landing humans on the Moon.

item.title: Spotify Sees Agentic AI as Growth Opportunity
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Spotify Claims It Is ‘Unusually Well-Positioned’ for an Agentic AI Takeover
Spotify’s co-CEO Gustav Söderström claims the company is ‘unusually well positioned’ for the rise of agentic AI. He argues Spotify’s platform can benefit from AI agents without losing direct consumer relationships. For example, AI assistants could request playlists, but Spotify’s systems would handle recommendations and playback. The company has partnered with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta’s Muse to integrate AI-driven features like AI-generated podcasts and personalized playlists. Söderström emphasized Spotify’s AI systems would process user data to refine recommendations, potentially revealing new insights about listener preferences. While Amazon blocked Meta’s Muse agents from accessing its platform due to privacy concerns, Spotify assures investors it won’t share proprietary user data. Instead, third-party agents would relay requests to Spotify’s own AI, which would ‘do the reasoning’ to decide what to play. The company is also developing AI features like a ChatGPT-like assistant and paid tools for AI-generated music. Söderström believes agentic AI will enhance Spotify’s role as a media service, with users interacting through agents rather than directly on the platform.

item.title: TSMC Seeks Equipment Free of Chinese Rare-Earth Magnets
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: TSMC is seeking chipmaking equipment that doesn't contain Chinese rare-earth magnets
TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, is seeking alternative machinery without rare-earth magnets to reduce reliance on China-dominated materials. Reuters reports that the Taiwanese firm has approached suppliers to find factory automation equipment using motors that avoid rare-earth elements like neodymium and dysprosium. China controls 70% of global rare earth mining and 95% of finished permanent magnets used in TSMC’s machines, according to the U.S. Geological Survey and International Energy Agency. In April 2025, China imposed export controls on seven rare earths and related magnets, requiring case-by-case approvals. The restrictions expanded in October 2025 to include more elements, processing tech, and products with Chinese-origin rare earths, though later suspended until November 2026. TSMC aims to mitigate production risks by exploring alternatives like induction motors and ferrite magnets, which offer trade-offs in efficiency and performance. Meanwhile, Taiwan and the U.S. are collaborating to develop domestic rare-earth production and alternative supply chains, with Taiwan planning a pilot line to meet 50% of its domestic demand. The U.S. also announced a $12 billion critical minerals stockpile to reduce China dependency.

item.title: Kevin Weil Launches Warp Sciences to Automate Drug Discovery Labs
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Former OpenAI science lead launches Warp Science to automate wet labs with robots
Kevin Weil, former OpenAI science lead, launched Warp Sciences, an AI startup automating lab work for drug discovery. The company raised $215 million at an $865 million valuation, with Lightspeed leading the round and IVP, Mayfield, Lux Capital, Premji Invest, and Menlo Ventures participating. Warp Sciences aims to reshift drug development work previously outsourced to Chinese contractors like WuXi AppTec, using robots trained by human chemists to perform lab tasks. The startup seeks to mitigate geopolitical supply-chain risks by enabling 24/7 operation of wet-lab processes, accelerating drug discovery through automation.

item.title: Apple Tests Under-Display Face ID for iPhone Duo 2
item.description:
Source: PCMag, Engadget, Digital Trends Original headline: Apple Tests iPhone Duo 2 with Under-Display Face ID to Replace Touch ID
Apple is testing under-display Face ID for the iPhone Duo 2, aiming to replace the current side-mounted Touch ID. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported that prototypes of the Duo 2 feature an under-display Face ID sensor and camera on the outer screen, potentially debuting in the second or third generation within two to three years. The upgrade addresses user complaints about the Touch ID setup, which is described as slow and awkward for left-handed users. The thin 5.2 mm chassis of the Duo made integrating the TrueDepth camera system challenging, and Apple sought uniformity across both displays, making Face ID on only one screen impractical. PCMag’s Eric Zeman praised the Duo’s hardware and performance, while Engadget noted the shift to Face ID since the iPhone X made returning to Touch ID a notable change. Gurman added that shrinking components, as seen in the iPhone 18 Pro’s Dynamic Island, may enable the under-display Face ID. The action button from the iPhone 15 Pro could also appear in future Duo models. The exact timeline for the Face ID upgrade remains uncertain, but sources confirm Apple is actively pursuing the technology to replace Touch ID.

item.title: Airbnb Bans Guest Chores Like Trash and Dishwashing
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: Airbnb Bans Some Check-Out Chores: No More Taking Out Trash, Washing Dishes
Airbnb is updating its guest policies to ban hosts from requesting specific chores. Effective Nov. 20, 2026, for bookings after that date, hosts may no longer ask guests to take out trash, wash dishes, strip bedding, or remove laundry from washing machines. Guests can still be asked to gather used towels or place dishes in the sink. Emptying trash cans or removing garbage is prohibited, though separating trash from recycling in indoor bins is allowed. Hosts cannot restrict use of listed amenities, such as air conditioning, but may ask guests to turn them off upon departure. Exceptions include disposing trash in animal-proof containers in bear country or limiting shower time during droughts. Airbnb emphasizes that most guests avoid unexpected chores, and such requests could harm their stay and host reviews.

item.title: Amazon Rebrands Kindle Unlimited as Kindle+ with Expanded Audiobook Library
item.description:
Source: Engadget, Digital Trends, Latest from Android Central
Amazon rebranded Kindle Unlimited as Kindle+ with expanded audiobook offerings. The $11.99 monthly service retains its 20-title borrowing limit but adds thousands of new audiobooks, including AI-narrated titles and ACX-produced content. Subscribers access ebooks, comics, magazines, and reading history without changes to borrowing mechanics or return policies. A new AI narration tool, Virtual Voice, allows KDP authors to create audiobooks for free, automatically including qualifying titles in the Kindle+ catalog. Traditional audiobooks via ACX remain available. The update is exclusive to U.S. subscribers initially, with international expansion planned. Critics question AI narration quality, but Amazon positions Kindle+ as a versatile service blending ebook and audiobook access. The service remains available through Kindle app and hardware without integration with Prime or Audible.
item.source: Engadget, Digital Trends, Latest from Android Central

item.title: Samsung Reports Galaxy Z8 Sales Surge Amid iPhone Duo Launch
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Samsung all but confirms iPhone Duo is goosing Galaxy Z8 sales
Samsung reports Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Z Fold 8 Ultra sales rose 45% compared to the Z Fold 7 in Europe. Search volume for the Z8 series spiked 460% in Europe the week of September 6-12, coinciding with the iPhone Duo's September 9 announcement. Samsung attributes the surge to increased interest in foldable phones following Apple's entry into the market. US preorders for the Z8 series are up 30% compared to last year. Samsung notes higher manufacturing ramp-up for wider foldables, likely driven by the iPhone Duo's impact. The company does not mention Apple or the iPhone Duo directly in its press release but links the sales boost to the timing of the iPhone announcement. Search volume for Z Fold 8 remained up 260% throughout September, the month of the phones' launch.

item.title: Russia's B-1 bomber clone set to get new avionics and a 'modular' architecture — new kit can be added later to boost longevity, not unlike the B-52 Stratofortress
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News
Russia's Tu-160M strategic bomber undergoes extensive modernization with 80% of its systems upgraded. The aircraft retains its Soviet-era appearance but features a modular avionics system allowing future electronic upgrades without full overhauls, similar to the B-52 Stratofortress. Tupolev General Director Yuri Abrosimov described the redesign as a 'new technological base' with digital enhancements, including updated radar, digital cockpits, improved communications, and NK-32-02 engines. Variable-geometry wings and four-engine configuration remain unchanged. Production delays pushed delivery of new Tu-160M aircraft to late 2025, with only two received by Russia's Aerospace Forces. Maintenance and production constraints may limit operational availability, as Ukrainian monitoring group AviVector reported seven of 18 bombers in combat and others in maintenance. Modular architecture's long-term effectiveness depends on compatible replacement technologies.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: VBoy Color emulator adds full color to Virtual Boy games
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: This emulator reimagines Nintendo’s Virtual Boy with a full color display
VBoy Color emulator adds full color to Virtual Boy games. Building on Red Viper's earlier work, the new project uses a tile-based palette system to assign distinct four-color palettes to each 8×8 tile in Virtual Boy scenes. This allows differentiation between objects like green pipes, grey platforms, and red bricks in games such as Mario Clash, which previously shared overlapping red hues. The Game Boy Color-inspired visuals create an alternate history where Nintendo adopted full-color displays instead of red LEDs. Enhanced contrast improves gameplay in titles like Jack Bros. and Vertical Force, where the original red-on-red display made distinguishing players from backgrounds difficult. The emulator's color packs enable detailed scene differentiation previously impossible with the original hardware's limited palette.

item.title: Galaxy Fit 4 leak shows similar design to predecessor
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Samsung’s Galaxy Fit 4 surfaces in new leak showing a familiar design
A new leak reveals the Galaxy Fit 4 retains a similar design to its predecessor. Android Authority obtained videos showing the device in black, white, and light blue colorways, featuring a rectangular display with curved edges, a physical button, silicone strap, and familiar sensor layout. Samsung has not confirmed the device or its specs, though previous leaks suggest Bluetooth Low Energy support and a Goodix GH3036 optical sensor for health tracking. The Galaxy Fit 3, launched in 2024 for around $60, offered affordable fitness tracking but lacked built-in GPS and had restrictive software. The leak shows few visible changes, leaving buyers to await details on potential improvements like GPS integration. Analysts note the design continuity may signal cautious development, with no clear hardware upgrades evident in the leak.

item.title: Spotify Adds QR Code Verification for Family Plan Users
item.description:
Source: The Verge, Engadget Original headline: Spotify Introduces QR Code Verification for Family Plan Users
Spotify has added a QR code verification system for Family Plan users, requiring members to scan the plan manager’s phone within seven days to maintain access. The update, announced during an earnings call, aims to enforce the rule that Family Plans are for people living in the same household. Co-CEO Alex Norström called the change a 'routine improvement,' noting the process will continue evolving as users find workarounds. The QR code refreshes every few seconds, prompting some to use video calls for remote scanning. Failure to complete verification results in a 12-month ban from joining other Family or Duo plans. Spotify allows users who miss the window to switch to an individual Premium subscription for $13 per month, compared to $22 for a Family Plan covering up to six accounts. While some users have criticized the new requirements, the company maintains the adjustments are necessary to ensure compliance with its terms of service.

item.title: Apple Introduces Badge to Highlight iPhone Duo-Optimized Apps
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Apple’s new badge makes it easy to find apps built for the iPhone Duo
Apple is introducing a new 'Made for iPhone Duo' badge to help users identify apps optimized for its foldable phone. The badge will appear on App Store pages starting October 23, alongside curated collections launching with the iPhone Duo in select markets. Examples include Netflix, which lets users browse clips on the outer screen before watching on the inner display, and Prime Video, which shows cast details on the bottom when partially folded. Productivity apps like Microsoft Word and Outlook offer desktop-class layouts, while Zoom displays shared content and participants side by side. Other apps such as Slack, Salesforce, NYT Cooking, Yelp, and travel apps will also utilize the extra space. Apple notes not all apps are ready yet, with more updates planned throughout the year. Existing iOS 27 apps may adjust automatically but won’t feel as tailored. The iPhone Duo, priced at $1,999 and already sold out through January, may delay developer urgency, though the badge aims to guide buyers toward compatible software.

item.title: Microsoft's AI System Outperforms Doctors in Complex Diagnoses
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, Gizmodo
Microsoft's AI diagnostic system MAI-DxO achieved 83% accuracy in complex medical cases, surpassing generalist physicians' 36% in simulations using New England Journal of Medicine cases. The system, which mimics a panel of doctors, leveraged improvements in AI models like GPT-5 and GPT-5.5. Microsoft's AI chief Mustafa Suleyman called the result a step toward 'medical superintelligence,' noting DxO's ability to question patients, order tests, and debate diagnoses. DxO reduced case costs by $3,000 compared to GPT-5 alone but showed less impact on emergency scenarios. The study, published in Science after initial preprint release, introduced the Sequential Diagnosis Benchmark (SDBench) for evaluating AI diagnostics. While DxO's performance on complex cases was nearly four times that of generalists without reference materials, experts caution real-world validation is needed. Microsoft plans clinical testing at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center and collaboration with Mayo Clinic for a 2027 healthcare foundation model release. Medical professionals emphasize AI tools are assistants, not replacements, with legal and ethical challenges remaining for adoption.

item.title: Etsy Tightens AI Rules to Combat Misleading Listings
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Etsy is cracking down on AI slop listings
Etsy is implementing stricter rules to limit AI-generated misleading listings. The platform requires all listings to include at least one unedited photo of the actual item against a real background, with all images accurately representing the product. AI tools can be used for non-first photos as long as they remain truthful. A pop-up will notify sellers if Etsy detects AI-generated images, prompting disclosure. Sellers must confirm that functional guides, like patterns or recipes, are original work, not AI-generated. Bot-created listings are prohibited, but AI art is allowed if disclosed. Buyers can request refunds if received items differ materially from listings. Etsy cites concerns from buyers unable to distinguish AI-generated content and sellers worried about unfair competition.

item.title: OpenAI Launches Decisions API to Compete in Fast Decision Models
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: OpenAI makes its Jev competitor widely available as decision model competition heats up
OpenAI launched its Decisions API, a fast, low-cost decision model, to compete with TypeSafe’s Jev, which became a $7.6 billion company. Jev models act as super classifiers, making quick choices with confidence ratings, replacing LLMs in workflows. Nikunj Handa, OpenAI’s product lead, noted the API reduces response times to 100-180 milliseconds, with plans for further optimization. The API, announced at OpenAI’s September 29 developer day, includes voice, visual modalities, and global latency improvements. Customers like Box and Speak reported faster processing, with Speak cutting action times from 1.4 seconds to 0.13 seconds. Benchmarks like AIM System One Index favor Liquid’s D1 Ultra and Base Lab’s Elephant-1, but Jev remains competitive, ranking third and seventh. TypeSafe’s Jev also excels in JevMan, a PacMan benchmark testing rapid decisions. OpenAI’s Luna model outperforms in image classification, though customers seek more flexibility. Handa highlighted potential for even faster APIs, like processing video frames. As decision models grow cheaper and faster, they may unlock new use cases, mirroring Jev’s namesake economist’s theory on resource efficiency.

item.title: Rare Pokémon Red prototype cartridge auctions for $25,000
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Extremely rare and 'previously undocumented' Pokémon Red prototype cartridge surfaces at auction, starting at $25,000
A prototype cartridge for Pokémon Red, a 1998 Game Boy game, is auctioning with a starting bid of $25,000. The cartridge, authenticated by PSA, contains 32KB of readable data matching the U.S. release version. PSA noted two header data changes that don't affect gameplay, including an incorrect Mask ROM version and checksum. The cartridge features a sticker with part number DMG-(F)KGDB-01, indicating it uses a previously undocumented development board. It includes a 16 megabit flash chip and is longer than standard Game Boy cartridges. The auction highlights its rarity, as the part number was previously linked to a 2000 development cartridge with similar components. Pokémon Red, alongside Green and Blue, sold over 31 million copies globally. The auction remains open, potentially reaching a higher price.

item.title: WhatsApp tests scheduled messages on iPhones with beta testers
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: WhatsApp’s long-awaited scheduling feature is finally being tested on iPhones
WhatsApp is testing scheduled messages on iPhones via TestFlight for beta testers using version 26.42.10.19. Users can schedule messages from 10 minutes to two weeks in advance, applicable to individual chats and groups. Scheduled messages work offline and remain encrypted. A dedicated section in chats allows reviewing or deleting messages before delivery, with no notification for deletions. Group chats have a limitation: new members won’t receive messages scheduled before their join date. The feature brings iOS and Android closer to parity, as Android beta testers received it earlier this month. WhatsApp hasn’t set a release date for stable users. The feature enables sending messages like midnight birthday alerts in advance.

item.title: As blockchain investing falls out of vogue, a16z Crypto rebrands as a16z Frontier
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch
Andreessen Horowitz renamed its digital asset unit from a16z Crypto to a16z Frontier, signaling a shift away from crypto-focused investing. The team, led by Chris Dixon, has raised nearly $10 billion since 2018, backing companies like Coinbase. The rebrand reflects broader challenges in advancing crypto’s utility beyond financial applications. a16z Frontier will now prioritize emerging technologies such as AI, robotics, and new networks connecting humans and machines. Dixon emphasized blockchain’s potential to provide economic capabilities to these networks. The firm’s general partners include Eddy Lazzarin and Guy Wuollet. Ali Yahya, the firm’s first crypto investor since 2017, has left the company.

item.title: Delta 2.0 Adds Retro Gaming Features to iPhone
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Delta 2.0 is finally here, and your iPhone just got a bigger retro gaming library
Delta 2.0 introduces Sega Genesis emulation and a redesigned Liquid Glass interface for iPhone. The update adds RetroAchievements for earning game milestones, animated controller skins, and customizable fast-forward speeds. It supports Apple’s foldable iPhone Duo, adapting controller layouts to different orientations and enabling Split View. Pokémon fans receive custom in-game content for Game Boy Advance titles, including event items and rare Pokémon in Pokémon Emerald. Experimental features include CRT visual filters, Epilogue GB/SN Operator accessory support for physical cartridge playback, and save file management. iPad multitasking improvements and bug fixes for SNES audio and NES launch issues are also included. The update enhances retro gaming customization, convenience, and authenticity through new features and optimizations.

item.title: Scientists create touchscreen fabric for wearable tech
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: This touchscreen is made from thread, and scientists want to put it in your clothes
Scientists at the National University of Singapore have developed a touchscreen woven into fabric, creating the world’s first garment-integrated display. The prototype features a 96 x 54-pixel screen embedded in a sleeve, capable of showing images, playing videos, running a calculator, and responding to touch. The technology integrates microelectronic components into flexible fibers, allowing the display to function without a rigid screen. The fabric maintains touch sensitivity and display quality after 50 machine-washing cycles and 1,000 bending cycles, remaining flexible and breathable. Potential applications include health monitoring, communication, and wearable computing. While current resolution is low and commercial release hasn’t been announced, the innovation marks progress toward interactive clothing that displays information without traditional screens. Researchers suggest future smart garments could replace bulky devices by embedding functionality directly into fabric.

item.title: Insta360 releases new e-ink wireless mics with expandable storage
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Insta360 adds expandable storage to its new e-ink wireless mics
Insta360's new wireless mics feature expandable microSD storage and customizable e-ink displays. The mics lack the Mic Pro's triple-mic array but offer 32-bit float recording with a microSD card. They connect directly to Insta360 cameras like the Luna Ultra and X6, recording 48kHz audio without a receiver. One receiver supports up to four mics and works with existing Mic Pro models. The base model sells for $80, with bundles including a receiver ($140) or transmitters and receiver ($250). Accessories include a button magnet, clip windshield, carry pouch, and USB-C phone adapter. The e-ink display allows user-uploaded images for branding, with options for solid colors or matching clothing. The new Mic is priced lower than the Mic Pro equivalent.

item.title: MSI Gets US Wi-Fi Router Ban Exemption
item.description:
Source: PCMag Original headline: MSI Receives Exemption to US Wi-Fi Router Ban
MSI has received an exemption to sell its Wi-Fi routers in the US after the Federal Communications Commission granted conditional approval for two Radix models, GRBE94 and GRBE36. The routers, designed for gaming, support Wi-Fi 7 technology with up to 10Gbps wired speeds. MSI still needs FCC equipment authorization to sell the products, with no release date provided. The exemption lasts until April 17, 2028, or 18 months, whichever comes first. The company joins other vendors like Asus, Netgear, Amazon’s eero, and SpaceX’s Starlink in temporary exemptions, as most router manufacturing occurs in Vietnam, Mexico, and Taiwan. MSI had previously announced plans for at least three new Radix routers at Computex, emphasizing low latency and high-speed connectivity for competitive gaming.

item.title: Atari VCS Software Store Closes in February 2027
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Retro Atari VCS platform will end with the closure of its software store in February 2027
Atari will shut down its VCS software store on February 1, 2027, ending support for the hybrid console-PC device. The company will release an OS update to let users migrate all functionality to their local machines, removing reliance on Atari infrastructure for authentication and software. Users can add software to their library via the official store until January 31, 2027. The Atari Homebrew App will be available during the transition, enabling users to build and share new games. The VCS, launched in 2021, featured an AMD Ryzen APU, 8GB RAM, and upgradable storage, running a custom Linux OS with retro games and streaming apps. Critics noted its high price, clunky PC mode, and noisy fan, recommending alternatives like mini PCs for similar performance at lower cost.

item.title: German Photographer Wins Nikon Small World Contest with Ink Droplet Image
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: Ink droplets in motion snag top prize in Nikon Small World contest
Ole Bielfeldt, a 25-year-old German experimental photographer, won the 2026 Nikon Small World photomicrography competition with an image of ink droplets being deposited on paper by an inkjet printer. His entry beat 1,802 submissions from 69 countries. Bielfeldt, who discovered a microscope during the COVID-19 lockdown, built custom tools to connect the microscope to his father’s camera and taught himself photomicrography. His winning image captured inkjet printer droplets mid-air, a challenge due to their speed. To freeze the action, he modified the printer to move paper under a stationary printhead and used a flash in a dark room as a shutter. He avoided AI, relying on traditional techniques. The image highlights his ability to transform everyday objects into striking visuals through meticulous setup and creativity.

item.title: Scientists Create System to Transmit Smells Over Internet
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Scientists have figured out how to send smells over the internet, and coffee is just the beginning
Scientists developed Scentronic, an AI-powered system that detects and transmits smells over the internet. Researchers from Ohio State University and Zhejiang Laboratory in China created the technology, published in Science Advances, to enable digital scent transmission. The system uses six gas sensors to identify chemical compounds in aromas, which are then converted into data and recreated via scented liquids and atomizers. The prototype supports five aromas: coffee, beer, red wine, cake, and orange. In tests with 14 volunteers, participants correctly identified recreated smells 73% of the time. While the technology cannot transmit actual odor molecules, it approximates scents using preloaded ingredients. Potential applications include enhancing online shopping, virtual reality, and remote fragrance testing. A prototype cup combines scent with flavored liquids for mixed-reality experiences. Researchers note limitations, as not all smells can be replicated, but the work suggests future digital experiences could engage more senses beyond sight and sound.

item.title: Book Reveals Collaborative Success Behind Batman: The Animated Series
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: ‘I Am the Night’ Spotlights the Unsung Heroes Who Made ‘Batman: The Animated Series’ Iconic
Daniel Dockery's book 'I Am the Night' challenges the myth of Bruce Timm as the sole architect of 'Batman: The Animated Series,' revealing the collaborative effort behind the show's success. The 304-page work includes interviews and archival research, detailing how the series evolved from a Saturday morning cartoon stigma to a cultural icon. Dockery highlights the creative team, including composer Shirley Walker, co-creator Eric Radomski, and writers Alan Burnett and Tom Ruegger, whose contributions were often overlooked. The book also explores production hurdles, such as outsourcing issues and the show's ratings success against 'Goof Troop.' Dockery emphasizes the show's impact on contemporaneous animated series like 'Captain Planet' and 'Gargoyles,' noting shared creative talent. The text delves into specific episodes, like 'Feat of Clay,' where director Kevin Altieri altered the script, leading to conflict with story editors. Dockery's research uncovers the show's less-than-ideal production history, including internal tensions and financial challenges. The book underscores the collective effort behind BTAS, moving beyond auteur worship to celebrate the 'creative village' that shaped the series.
